How this book matches your exam. Research check: Business Studies 0450 is examined for the last time in 2026. From March 2027 (India) and June 2027 (elsewhere) it is replaced by Cambridge IGCSE Business 0264. These books are written for 0264, and the content also covers almost all of 0450.

0264 topics:

  1. Understanding business activity
  2. People in business
  3. Marketing
  4. Operations management (new: 4.2 Technology and production; 4.3 Sustainable production)
  5. Financial information and decisions
  6. External influences on business activity

Assessment:

  • Paper 1 (Short Answer and Data Response): 1 h 30 min, 80 marks, 50%, four compulsory questions.
  • Paper 2 (Case Study): 1 h 30 min, 80 marks, 50%, four compulsory questions on a case-study insert.
  • 0264 assessment objectives: knowledge 35%, application 30%, analysis 22%, evaluation 13%. Application has risen, so always use the business in the question.

This book covers Topic 1.1–1.3. Every calculation was checked by computer. The marking guides are our own, not official Cambridge mark schemes.

Unit 1 of 10: The Purpose of Business Activity

Key ideas

  • Needs: goods and services essential for survival. Wants: goods and services people would like to have.
  • Scarcity: there are not enough resources to meet all wants, so choices must be made.
  • Opportunity cost: the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.
  • The purpose of business: to combine factors of production (land, labour, capital, enterprise) to produce goods and services that satisfy needs and wants.

Worked examples

Example 1: a bakery combines flour (land), bakers (labour), ovens (capital) and the owner's ideas (enterprise) to make bread.

Example 2: a business choosing to buy a van instead of a new oven: the opportunity cost is the oven.

Example 3: a phone is a want for most; clean water is a need.

10-mark exam-style question

Ayesha runs a small café. (a) Define opportunity cost. [2] (b) Identify the four factors of production Ayesha uses, with an example of each. [4] (c) Ayesha has $5 000 and must choose between a new coffee machine and an advertising campaign. Explain the opportunity cost of buying the machine. [2] (d) Explain why scarcity forces Ayesha to make choices. [2]

Answers: (a) The next best alternative (B1) given up when making a choice (B1). (b) Land: the café premises; labour: baristas; capital: the coffee machine; enterprise: Ayesha's risk-taking and organisation (B4). (c) The advertising campaign she cannot now afford (B1); this could have attracted more customers (B1). (d) Her money / resources are limited (B1), so she cannot buy everything she wants (B1).

Common mistakes

  1. Defining opportunity cost as "the cost of something". 2. Calling money a factor of production. 3. Not applying to the café. 4. Needs vs wants confused. 5. Listing factors without examples.

Quick recall

  1. Next best alternative forgone? 2. Four factors? 3. A need? 4. Why choose? 5. Enterprise means?

Answers: 1) Opportunity cost. 2) Land, labour, capital, enterprise. 3) Food or water. 4) Scarcity. 5) Organising resources and taking risks.
